title: RE4's Director Said He'd Cut Off His Head If It Hit PS2
hook: In a 2002 interview Shinji Mikami said he'd cut his own head off if Resident Evil 4 ever left GameCube. Capcom announced the PS2 version on October 31, 2004, before the GameCube disc had even shipped. Would you have stayed loyal to the Cube?
script: Did you know the director of Resident Evil Four said he would cut off his own head if it ever came to PlayStation Two? In a Japanese magazine interview in the summer of two thousand two, Shinji Mikami promised the game would only ever be on GameCube. If it showed up on another console, he said, he would cut his head off. In Japanese the phrase is closer to saying he would lose his job, but the translation stuck. That November, Capcom announced five GameCube games now remembered as the Capcom Five. The list included Viewtiful Joe and Killer Seven, and both of those also ended up on PlayStation Two. Within two months Capcom admitted only Resident Evil Four was actually locked to GameCube. Then, on Halloween of two thousand four, Capcom announced the game was coming to PlayStation Two as well. The GameCube version had not even shipped yet. It finally arrived in January of the next year, and the PlayStation Two version followed that October. Mikami kept his head. Years later he admitted his bet on Nintendo was completely wrong. He said he had told Capcom's chairman they would have to fire him first. The original has since sold more than ten million copies across its versions. Would you have stayed loyal to the GameCube? Follow for more gaming history.
